title: Holistic unit-econ heuristics for dynamic batching, KV-caching defaults, and quantization prescreen
author: Priya Nair
description:
Motivation: production customers see wide variance in per-request unit economics depending on payload distribution, prefix repetition and model quantization. Manual tuning (batch sizes, KV cache TTLs, quant profile selection) is error-prone and often reactive. This PR introduces a small, conservative automation that sets default heuristics for batching and KV-caching and provides a quantization prescreen that recommends model-quant pairs with estimated token-cost delta. The goal is safe, backwards-compatible defaults that reduce tail cost by targeting common patterns while providing operators a transparent simulation-backed recommendation before changes are applied.

Summary of changes: 
- Heuristic controller that computes per-route defaults based on sampled request histograms (payload length, prefix reuse, latency SLO). Defaults influence: continuous batching target size, batching latency cushion, KV cache TTL and prefix fingerprint sampling rate.
- Quantization prescreen runner: offline simulation harness that runs candidate quant settings (int8/int4/relaxed FP16) against a small corpus and emits an estimated quality delta + cost delta. Results are surfaced to the console and to the unit-econ dashboard.
- Unit-econ estimator integration: lightweight cost estimator that combines model latency profiles, batch size, and token estimates to show projected per-1M-token cost for recommended defaults.
- Safe rollout: new "safe-mode" flag prevents any automatic application of defaults in Dedicated/Private; defaults are suggestions unless operator flips the apply flag.

Checklist: 
- [x] Design doc + simulation plan (linked Linear ENG-4821)
- [x] Unit tests for controller heuristics and prescreen harness
- [x] Integration tests exercising sample route and reporting to the unit-econ estimator 
- [x] E2E smoke against real traffic replay in the benchmark-lab (no regressions)
- [x] Console UI hooks (backend only) for recommendations
- [x] Rollout plan + rollback path documented

Why this is conservative: defaults are computed from a 24h sampled histogram and bounded by policy caps; any recommendation labelled "apply-recommended" must be explicitly enabled per-organization. The prescreen reports an expected quality delta and includes a bootstrap validation step using customer-provided eval prompts if available.

Commit summary: 
- Add heuristic controller and sampling pipeline
- Add quant prescreen harness and simulation runner
- Integrate estimator with console recommendation API
- Add unit & integration tests; update observability events and metrics

Files changed (high level): 
- runtime/controller/unit_econ_heuristic.py (new) - core controller, sampling, default computation
- runtime/quant/prescreen_runner.py (new) - simulation harness for quant profiles
- runtime/estimator/cost_estimator.py (new) - unit-econ estimator and projection APIs
- console/api/recommendations.py - new endpoints for recommendations and prescreen results
- benchmark-lab/replays/unit_econ_smoke.json - sample traffic used in tests
- tests/unit/test_heuristics.py, tests/integration/test_prescreen_integration.py
- metrics/events.yaml - new observability events for recommendations and user actions

Testing and CI: ran full unit and integration suite on benchmark-lab; CI showed intermittent timeout in an unrelated flaky e2e (replayed and resolved). All required checks passed before merge. Performance validation: median downstream latency increased by <0.5ms for typical small-batch workloads; estimated per-1M-token cost decreased 4-12% for routes with >30% prefix reuse.

Rollout plan: stage behind feature flag in staging -> canary on 5% of traffic with recommendations shown but not applied -> operator review flow in Console -> 25% auto-apply (if explicit opt-in) -> full apply only after 14 days of monitoring. Rollback: flip feature flag or set safe-mode to true to revert defaults.

Related: references to prior cost automation PRs and research notes. Linear: ENG-4821 for design, ENG-4890 for prescreen evaluation.

Notes for reviewers: pay attention to sampling window sizing and policy cap logic in unit_econ_heuristic.py; the quant prescreen is intentionally conservative and uses a weighted quality metric, not raw perplexity. If you want to test locally, see instructions in runtime/quant/README.md included in changes.

review_comments:
Ethan Kline: Nice end-to-end. Two asks: (1) tighten the policy cap math so a single long-tail request doesn't blow up batch targets, and (2) add a small opt-out for private customers.
Author (Priya): tightened cap math and exposed safe-mode opt-out. Updated tests.

Marta Ruiz: Can we be explicit about how we estimate quality delta for quantization? Need reproducible metric.
Author: prescreen now outputs a weighted 'quality_score' based on eval set ROC-AUC + human-labeled subset; details in runtime/quant/README.md.

Liam O'Connor: CI showed intermittent e2e timeout; you addressed by increasing replay timeout in benchmark-lab. Approving once green.
Author: increased timeout and added retry guard for flaky network call.
release_notes: Introduce heuristic-driven defaults for batching and KV cache and a quant prescreen that recommends safe quant profiles with projected unit-econ impact. Recommendations are opt-in by default; no automatic changes without operator approval.
deployment_notes: Feature gated behind 'unit_econ_recommendations' feature flag. To enable auto-apply for a workspace set 'apply_recommendations' in org config; otherwise recommendations are readonly. Safe-mode prevents auto-application in Dedicated/Private by default.
observability_impact: Adds recommendation events (recommendation.generated, recommendation.applied, recommendation.reverted) and cost projection metrics. Dashboards updated in observability-pack.
notes_for_ops: If operators see regressions after applying recommendations, set org-level safe-mode=true to stop auto-applies and file SUP-1304 for assisted rollback. A replay script scripts/simulate_prescreen.sh can be used to validate changes against archived traffic.
